title: Queen Suriyothai
summary: Queen consort of King Maha Chakkraphat of Ayutthaya, traditionally said to have died in the Burmese-Siamese war of 1548 after riding an elephant into battle to shield her husband. Reported dates conflict and some scholars question the story; one suggests a princess fought instead. A monument stands on the Makham Yong plain, believed to be the battle site, north of Ayutthaya.

uncertainty.note: Two sources give 1548 for the war and the traditional death; a third opens its account with 1549. The ayutthaya-history.com page says reported dates relating to her, and some Royal Chronicles, are in conflict. No birth date appears in the opened sources.

where.modern_name: Queen Suriyothai Monument, Makham Yong Plain, north of Ayutthaya, Phra Nakhon Si Ayutthaya Province, Thailand (monument at the believed battle site, unveiled 1995)
where.historical_name: Makham Yong Plain, near the capital of the Ayutthaya kingdom, in the reign of King Chakkraphat (1548-1569) per ayutthaya-history.com

importance.justification: The sources treat her as a Thai national symbol and the best known woman of the Ayutthaya period.

reviewer_note: Legendary or contested figure. No museum, university or government page could be opened; ayutthaya-history.com is classed reference by the agent (a long-running research site on Ayutthaya) and should be confirmed. Birth date and whether the fighter was the queen or a princess are not settled in the sources. The pin marks the monument at the believed site, not a surveyed battlefield. Withdrawn from the globe: all sources are hobbyist or commercial sites; needs a museum, university or government source.
